---
title: "Discover geo.admin assets with STAC"
description: "Search collections, inspect items and assets, then download explicitly."
---

<div class="toolbox-kind">Recipe · STAC v1 verified 2026-10-04</div>

## Purpose

Use a stable collection ID plus an optional date and bbox/polygon to discover assets. Keep discovery separate from download:

```text
collection → search → inspect items → inspect assets → select → download
```

This generic workflow is useful for tiled products such as SWISSIMAGE and swissSURFACE3D, and for collections whose item structure is not yet known. For G1/K4 administrative boundaries, use the much shorter [Swiss administrative geometries workflow](../resources/swiss-geometries.qmd): choose the product and date, fetch one national GPKG, then open the required layer. G1/K4 do not require a spatial search or tile selection.

The verified catalog root is:

```text
https://data.geo.admin.ch/api/stac/v1/
```

geo.admin recommends STAC v1; v0.9 is deprecated. The service exposes GET and POST search, cursor pagination and WGS84 search geometries. Keep the version explicit and recheck the root document before changing it.

## Packages

:::: {.panel-tabset}
### R

```r
library(tidyverse)
library(httr2)
library(jsonlite)
library(sf)
library(here)

raw_dir <- here("input", "raw")
stac_root <- "https://data.geo.admin.ch/api/stac/v1/"
```

### Python

```python
import json
from pathlib import Path

import geopandas as gpd
import pandas as pd
import requests
from shapely.geometry import mapping

raw_dir = Path("input/raw")
stac_root = "https://data.geo.admin.ch/api/stac/v1/"
```
::::

## Inspect the collection

Start with collection metadata and its `items` link. This confirms the identifier, temporal/spatial extent, provider, license link and available projection summaries.

:::: {.panel-tabset}
### R

```r
collection_id <- "ch.bfs.historisierte-administrative_grenzen_g1"
collection_url <- paste0(stac_root, "collections/", collection_id)

response <- request(collection_url) |>
  req_perform()
resp_check_status(response)

collection <- resp_body_json(response, simplifyVector = FALSE)
collection[c("id", "title", "description", "extent", "license")]
collection$links
```

### Python

```python
collection_id = "ch.bfs.historisierte-administrative_grenzen_g1"
collection_url = f"{stac_root}collections/{collection_id}"

response = requests.get(collection_url, timeout=30)
response.raise_for_status()
collection = response.json()

{key: collection.get(key) for key in ["id", "title", "description", "extent", "license"]}
collection["links"]
```
::::

## Search all pages

Pagination uses the `href` of the JSON link whose `rel` is `next`. After the first request, follow that URL exactly because it carries an opaque cursor.

:::: {.panel-tabset}
### R

```r
get_stac_pages <- function(url, query = list()) {
  features <- list()

  repeat {
    request_current <- request(url)
    if (length(query) > 0) {
      request_current <- do.call(req_url_query, c(list(request_current), query))
    }

    response <- req_perform(request_current)
    resp_check_status(response)
    page <- resp_body_json(response, simplifyVector = FALSE)
    features <- c(features, page$features)

    next_links <- Filter(
      function(link) identical(link$rel, "next"),
      page$links
    )
    if (length(next_links) == 0) break

    url <- next_links[[1]]$href
    query <- list()
  }

  features
}

search_stac <- function(collection, datetime = NULL, bbox = NULL,
                        intersects = NULL, sortby = NULL, limit = 100) {
  stopifnot(is.null(bbox) || is.null(intersects))

  query <- list(collections = collection, limit = limit)
  if (!is.null(datetime)) query$datetime <- datetime
  if (!is.null(bbox)) query$bbox <- paste(bbox, collapse = ",")
  if (!is.null(intersects)) {
    query$intersects <- toJSON(intersects, auto_unbox = TRUE)
  }
  if (!is.null(sortby)) query$sortby <- sortby

  get_stac_pages(paste0(stac_root, "search"), query)
}
```

### Python

```python
def get_stac_pages(url, params=None):
    features = []

    while url is not None:
        response = requests.get(url, params=params, timeout=30)
        response.raise_for_status()
        page = response.json()
        features.extend(page["features"])

        next_link = next(
            (link for link in page["links"] if link["rel"] == "next"),
            None,
        )
        url = next_link["href"] if next_link else None
        params = None

    return features


def search_stac(
    collection, datetime=None, bbox=None, intersects=None, sortby=None, limit=100
):
    if bbox is not None and intersects is not None:
        raise ValueError("Use bbox or intersects, not both")

    params = {"collections": collection, "limit": limit}
    if datetime is not None:
        params["datetime"] = datetime
    if bbox is not None:
        params["bbox"] = ",".join(map(str, bbox))
    if intersects is not None:
        params["intersects"] = json.dumps(intersects)
    if sortby is not None:
        params["sortby"] = sortby

    return get_stac_pages(f"{stac_root}search", params=params)
```
::::

## Search by exact date and bbox

STAC spatial filters use WGS84 longitude/latitude in the order `xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax`.

:::: {.panel-tabset}
### R

```r
bbox <- c(5.9, 45.8, 10.5, 47.9)

items <- search_stac(
  collection = collection_id,
  datetime = "2024-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  bbox = bbox
)
```

### Python

```python
bbox = [5.9, 45.8, 10.5, 47.9]

items = search_stac(
    collection=collection_id,
    datetime="2024-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    bbox=bbox,
)
```
::::

For historized administrative boundaries, skip this generic search and use the dedicated G1/K4 workflow. A dated G1/K4 item covers the complete national dataset, so a bbox does not reduce the downloaded file.

## Search with a polygon

Transform the input geometry to WGS84 before serializing it as GeoJSON.

:::: {.panel-tabset}
### R

```r
area <- st_read(file.path(raw_dir, "study_area.gpkg"), quiet = TRUE) |>
  st_transform(4326) |>
  summarise()

# sf deliberately writes the geometry; jsonlite then reads the GeoJSON structure.
area_file <- tempfile(fileext = ".geojson")
st_write(area, area_file, driver = "GeoJSON", quiet = TRUE)
area_geojson <- read_json(area_file, simplifyVector = FALSE)
unlink(area_file)

intersects <- area_geojson$features[[1]]$geometry
items <- search_stac(collection_id, intersects = intersects)
```

### Python

```python
area = gpd.read_file(raw_dir / "study_area.gpkg").to_crs(4326)
intersects = mapping(area.geometry.union_all())

items = search_stac(collection_id, intersects=intersects)
```
::::

The search finds items whose footprints intersect the geometry; it does not clip downloaded data.

## Inspect items and assets

Flatten metadata for inspection, but retain the original item JSON when provenance matters.

:::: {.panel-tabset}
### R

```r
items_table <- map_dfr(items, function(item) {
  tibble(
    item_id = item$id,
    datetime = if (is.null(item$properties$datetime)) NA_character_
      else item$properties$datetime,
    start_datetime = if (is.null(item$properties$start_datetime)) NA_character_
      else item$properties$start_datetime,
    end_datetime = if (is.null(item$properties$end_datetime)) NA_character_
      else item$properties$end_datetime,
    title = item$properties$title
  )
})

assets_table <- map_dfr(items, function(item) {
  imap_dfr(item$assets, function(asset, asset_key) {
    tibble(
      item_id = item$id,
      asset_key = asset_key,
      title = asset$title,
      media_type = asset$type,
      epsg = if (is.null(asset[["proj:epsg"]])) NA_integer_
        else asset[["proj:epsg"]],
      gsd = if (is.null(asset$gsd)) NA_real_ else asset$gsd,
      href = asset$href,
      checksum = if (is.null(asset[["checksum:multihash"]])) NA_character_
        else asset[["checksum:multihash"]]
    )
  })
})

items_table
assets_table |> select(item_id, asset_key, title, media_type, epsg)
```

### Python

```python
items_table = pd.DataFrame(
    {
        "item_id": item["id"],
        "datetime": item["properties"].get("datetime"),
        "start_datetime": item["properties"].get("start_datetime"),
        "end_datetime": item["properties"].get("end_datetime"),
        "title": item["properties"].get("title"),
    }
    for item in items
)

assets_table = pd.DataFrame(
    {
        "item_id": item["id"],
        "asset_key": asset_key,
        "title": asset.get("title"),
        "media_type": asset.get("type"),
        "epsg": asset.get("proj:epsg"),
        "gsd": asset.get("gsd"),
        "href": asset["href"],
        "checksum": asset.get("checksum:multihash"),
    }
    for item in items
    for asset_key, asset in item["assets"].items()
)

items_table
assets_table[["item_id", "asset_key", "title", "media_type", "epsg"]]
```
::::

For G1/K4 dated items, the GPKG contains all administrative layers. GeoJSON assets are split by level (`gemeinde`, `bezirk`, `kanton`, `land`, `see`). Prefer the GPKG for normal spatial analysis and inspect its layers after download.

## Select and download explicitly

This example requires exactly one GPKG asset. Change the filter rather than silently choosing the first match.

:::: {.panel-tabset}
### R

```r
selected <- assets_table |>
  filter(media_type == "application/geopackage+sqlite3")

stopifnot(nrow(selected) == 1)
dir.create(raw_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

destination <- file.path(raw_dir, basename(selected$href))
request(selected$href) |>
  req_perform(path = destination)

st_layers(destination)
```

### Python

```python
selected = assets_table.loc[
    assets_table["media_type"] == "application/geopackage+sqlite3"
]
if len(selected) != 1:
    raise ValueError(f"Expected one GPKG asset, found {len(selected)}")

raw_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
asset_url = selected.iloc[0]["href"]
destination = raw_dir / Path(asset_url).name

with requests.get(asset_url, stream=True, timeout=120) as response:
    response.raise_for_status()
    with destination.open("wb") as file:
        for chunk in response.iter_content(chunk_size=1024 * 1024):
            file.write(chunk)

gpd.list_layers(destination)
```
::::

Save the STAC response alongside acquired data when a reproducible record of item and asset selection is important. Asset metadata may include a multihash checksum; validating that checksum requires decoding its algorithm prefix, so do not label it as a plain SHA-256 without checking.

## Verified administrative collections

| Collection | Intended use | Verified assets |
|---|---|---|
| `ch.bfs.historisierte-administrative_grenzen_g1` | Default administrative geometry for analysis and thematic mapping | GPKG EPSG:2056; per-layer GeoJSON; Shapefile archive |
| `ch.bfs.historisierte-administrative_grenzen_k4` | More generalized, lightweight small-scale mapping | GPKG; per-layer GeoJSON; Shapefile archive; collection advertises EPSG:2056 and 4326 |

Prefer GPKG or GeoJSON. Shapefile is listed only because the catalog exposes it, not as the recommended default.
